name: Indus Towers Ltd
title: Indus Towers Ltd - 534816 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Indus Towers Q4 FY26: reported EBITDA INR 44.6bn (+1.6% YoY, 55.1% margin) and FY26 final dividend of INR 14/share distributing full-year FCF of INR 37.6bn.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR 81bn (+4.8% YoY) and core rental revenue INR 53.1bn (+5.4% YoY), with co-locations up 5.6% YoY. Reported EBITDA was flat-to-up YoY but down 1% QoQ, held back by a Q4 one-time settlement hit to revenue, a Q3 positive one-off in other expenses, and higher seasonal maintenance spend. Full-year PAT fell 28.1% YoY to INR 71.4bn because FY25 carried a INR 51bn receivables write-back; normalised EBITDA and PAT grew 11.4% and 13%. The Board recommended a final dividend of INR 14/share, distributing the full FY26 free cash flow, with management guiding to a steady and progressive payout going forward.

financial_highlights.value: INR 11.1bn in Q4; INR 37.6bn in FY26

segments.name: Towers and co-locations (India)
segments.commentary: Q4 added 4,892 macro towers and 6,192 co-locations, taking the base to about 264,500 towers and 428,000 co-locations (+6.1% and +5.6% YoY). Tenancy ratio stable at 1.62; leaner-tower co-locations exceed 14,000, portfolio about 442,000 including leaner towers.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: Energy revenue fell QoQ on cost optimisation and seasonal energy cost decline; energy margin -3.6% in Q4 vs -5.2% a year earlier. Solar access added at about 2,500 sites in Q4, taking the total to about 42,400; diesel consumption down about 7% YoY.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Operating licence secured in Zambia with on-ground execution starting; Uganda and Nigeria in final regulatory stages. Commercial frameworks and initial orders in place with the anchor customer; capex for Africa described as not significant initially.

segments.name: Non-tower / DAS / IBS
segments.commentary: Company says it reached leadership in IBS in Q4; DAS deployments picked up in metros, tunnels and highways. No figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Final dividend of INR 14/share recommended; management says the endeavour is steady and progressive distribution, with no minimum payout formula (dividend policy: FCF distributed at year-end, subject to working capital).
Management does not give forward numbers; says order book is healthy for the next few quarters with growth-oriented capex (about 70% of capex is growth, about 25% replacement/maintenance).
Full-year EBITDA margin said to be in line with the 55%-plus expectation.
Africa tower deployment expected to begin soon in Zambia, with ramp-up as approvals come through in Uganda and Nigeria.
capex_capacity: Q4 tower additions 4,892 and co-location additions 6,192; FY26 full-year additions about 15,200 towers and 22,500 co-locations.
Over 85% of sites digitally connected (fuel sensors, backhaul monitoring, smart meters, power equipment).
About 531,000 5G BTSs installed in the base; growth expected from loading on existing towers, with selective tower footprint expansion later.
Management flagged supply-side tightness in tower materials linked to LPG availability and West Asia conflict, affecting deployment timelines and costs.
demand_pricing: Core revenue growth muted by Q4 FY25 one-time reconciliation benefit (about 2.1pp of base) and a Q4 FY26 one-time settlement; management cited organic service revenue growth of about 5-5.5% YoY after adjusting for an Airtel tower acquisition.
Annual escalations of about 2.5% cited as a revenue driver.
Management said a major customer's contract expiries affect only a very small portion of the portfolio; some Jio tenancies have expired but are still operating, with minor churn.
Management expects tenancy ratio trend to change as second anchor customer ramps; cannot give a directional outlook.
Diesel-price pass-through is said to be billed on actuals with no lag; industrial (bulk) diesel price rise does not affect the company's retail diesel purchases.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about the FCF from last year's VI dues reversal, now that FY26 FCF is almost fully distributed, and what capex guidance applies?
qa_highlights.answer: Board evaluated FCF and desired debt levels and chose to distribute FY26 FCF; capex about 70% growth, 25% replacement, and no forward numbers given, with a healthy order book.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a formal dividend policy, and is there a minimum payout?
qa_highlights.answer: Policy is on the website: the Board considers distributing year-end FCF, subject to working capital and other conditions; no minimum payout amount is specified.

qa_highlights.question: Why has FY25 cash not been released, given earlier comments about distributing it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Board did not compartmentalise cash by year; it assessed full FCF and debt levels, with total distributions of about INR 37-38bn.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 maintenance spend a one-off or a structural reset as towers age?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonality (clear-weather Q3/Q4 and pre-monsoon preparation) plus a deliberate tower-strengthening programme; said cost per tower has fallen over 3-4 years and the base is not reset.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the sequential EBITDA decline and per-tower drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 revenue hit by a one-time settlement; Q3 had a positive one-off in other expenses; network maintenance up 5.6% QoQ; full-year margin still on track at 55%-plus.

qa_highlights.question: Why are single-tenancy tower additions rising and what is the Vodafone rollout impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said co-location additions exceeded tower additions in Q3 and Q4; some towers move from other tower companies to Indus (net addition), so a direct split is not possible.

qa_highlights.question: When will Africa operations start, and will NOC be local or in India?
qa_highlights.answer: First tower in Zambia expected very soon, well within six months; NOC location not yet decided.

qa_highlights.question: Do the Jio tower contract expiries lead to churn, and were renewals at the same terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Some expired tenancies still operate; very minor percentage churned; renewals continue on the same terms, with no incremental concessions mentioned in response.

risks_watch: Customer financial health and non-renewal of expired tenancies (management says a small portion of the portfolio), and tenancy ratio trend as second anchor customer ramps.
Supply-chain tightness and cost inflation from the West Asia conflict and LPG availability, affecting tower deployments and costs.
Maintenance cost trend on the aging portfolio, and whether Q4 maintenance spending repeats.
Dividend sustainability versus capex and Africa investment, plus debt levels after the Airtel tower acquisition funding.
Energy margin (-3.6% in Q4) under diesel and grid price changes; smart meter mandate by CEA.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and the order book, but guarded on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to give FY27/FY28 guidance and cited supply-chain uncertainty. Evasive on the dividend's relation to FY25 cash and on tenancy trends, and defensive on the Q4 EBITDA decline, which it attributed to one-offs and seasonality.
key_quotes: So I don't think the cost base is fundamentally reset.
Our industry-leading tenancy ratio was stable at 1.62.
The endeavor would be to follow a steady and progressive distribution.
So honestly speaking, I don't think the Board compartmentalized the cash flows in that category.

adds.what: Q4 FY26 macro tower additions of 4,892 and 6,192 co-locations (FY26 full-year about 15,200 towers and 22,500 co-locations already added)
Zambia tower deployment starting on-ground under operating licence (Uganda and Nigeria pending regulatory approvals)

growth.why: Management gives no forward revenue number; full-year EBITDA margin held at 55%-plus, and Q4 revenue grew 4.8% YoY with co-locations up 5.6%, backed by a healthy order book, about 70% growth capex, FY26 additions of about 15,200 towers and 22,500 co-locations, and Zambia rollout starting with an anchor customer, though no specific forward capacity numbers were given.
